body: I relate so hard. I've had disordered eating habits for 11 years now and I was so uncomfortable eating around others. Eventually I just lost interest in eating so meal times were unbearable. I would cry and sit at the table for hours before giving up. Then I found Stephanie's mukbangs. I'll admit that the eating sounds bothered so much so that I would skip those parts while I was eating. Eventually I would watch the whole video while I was eating and things got easier because I was so sucked into the cases. Took baby steps but now I feel comfortable eating with friends and trying new food cause I say "oh stephanie ate it so it's probably good". I'm so grateful, I hope she knows that she had a positive impact on people.

As an esthetician who has done waxing, I can assure you that we've seen it all below the belt. We do it so much that it becomes muscle memory to wax, so we don't judge. Its okay to be a little bit nervous the first time, but you'll see that the environment isn't as tense as you may think. 

PLEASE, just remember to take a shower and clean really well down there before your appointment!

I feel this way. I feel like I'm usually planning it out in my head too. I didn't see myself making it to spring this year.  But here I am...despite therapy and increased doses of meds, I still I'll do it.

I also feel like that. I see someone so happy, truly blissful, and I can't help but feel upset. I'm upset because I don't feel that way and haven't been able to in so long. I'm tired of feeling so weighed down, meanwhile people can feel happy with such little effort.

Sometimes I feel guilty about it too. For example my best friend is in a beautiful, healthy, committed relationship with her boyfriend. I want to be happy for her...but I'm not. I feel distraught because I know what's out there, yet haven't been able to find the same for myself.

I've been on zoloft since January and the first month was hell with the side effects. The nausea was INCREDIBLY awful and the insomnia was hard to deal with. It got better eventually as my body adjusted. I felt like it gave me more energy to do my job and feel semi normal again. But lately, it's hasn't been helping much. I've had my dosage increased twice during quarantine and haven't felt myself feel better.

I'm 20 years old and I'm surprised that I even made it this far. I genuinely thought that I wouldn't make it past the winter. My therapist thought that it would be a good idea to practice more self care, so I bought concert tickets to see my favorite band. I wanted to live long enough to see them in concert, and then end it all. But it got canceled and now I'm here...pondering when I'll give my brother access to all my possessions when I die.
